items.reason: setup() initializes Serial, vibration input D2, LED D13, buzzer D6, fan PWM D5, TM1637 with CLK=D4/DIO=D3, and loop samples A0/A1 each tick.

Normal state is never produced: with vibration false, io_1>=0 always true, and io_0>=0 always true (ADC 0..1023), so stateCode becomes 1 (overload) unconditionally; stateCode 0 is unreachable in the normal branch.
Overload is not distinguished by a current threshold; any non-negative ADC reading yields stateCode=1, so overload is reported even at zero current and there is no load-based condition.
When temperature ADC >= 30, stateCode=3 and fan PWM is set to 255 on D5, enabling cooling.
Vibration true sets faultCode=1 and stateCode=4, driving buzzer tone 2000Hz on D6 and LED on; fault code is reported via serial.
The vibration branch is checked first and overrides temperature/current, so mechanical fault takes priority when simultaneous; buzzer and faultCode set accordingly.
TM1637 only shows a single value (stateCode or 40) each tick; there is no rotation among current, temperature, and state number.

Green LED (io_2) is driven by parking sensor state (io_7 && io_6>=5), not by entrance approach (io_5). Entrance detection only affects red LED io_1. So green does not light when a vehicle approaches the entrance.

Buzzer frequency is graded by parking distance (2000/1200/800/400 Hz across <5, 2-10, 10-30, >=30 cm bands) and LEDs reflect parking state, satisfying graded buzzer/LED feedback when entering the spot.
When parking valid and distance <5cm, io_3=2000 Hz continuously via tone() each tick; noTone only when freq<=0, so alarm persists while condition holds.
Button edge detection increments mode 0->1->2->0; display selects entrance distance (mode 0), parking distance (mode 1), or occupancyCount (mode 2).

When the count changes, displayCount(occupiedCount) writes the count digit to the TM1637 via the bit-banged driver.

RESET command (ALL or 1/2/3) sets emptySince to now and clears restockReported for the selected shelves, resetting the empty timers.

When temp reaches/exceeds targetTemp the comparison is false, so io_1 is false and D10 driven LOW.

When modeIsSetting is true, io_8 is floor of targetTemp and shown on TM1637.

Low counter increments each 10ms tick when temp <=36; at 6000 ticks (~60s) alarmActive sets LED, buzzer tone, and serial prints incubation abnormal.

setup() initializes Serial, A0/A1 as inputs, D2 input, D5 output, D6 output, D13 output, and TM1637 with CLK=4/DIO=3; loop() samples all three sensors every 10ms and runs the model, so real-time monitoring is established.
When temperature io_1>=0 and <30 and current io_0>=0, stateCode is set to 1 (normal); otherwise 0. This is the normal branch of the state machine.
When current io_0>=0 (and not overtemp), stateCode=1 is the overload state distinct from normal 0; the model maps a non-negative current reading to overload.
When io_1>=30 stateCode=3 (overheat), and the model sets io_3=255 for stateCode==3, which is written to PWM D5 via analogWrite, enabling the fan.
On vibration (io_2 true, edge or level), stateCode=4 and faultCode=1; faultCode!=0 drives tone 2000Hz on D6 and serial fault_code output, giving priority alarm and fault code.

The vibration branch is checked first (if sysml_lazy_1) before the temperature/current branches, so when vibration coincides with overheat/overload, stateCode=4 and faultCode=1 take precedence, producing the 2000Hz alarm and fault code.

The TM1637 only ever displays a single value (io_6 = stateCode, or 40 when faultCode!=0); there is no rotation among current, temperature, and state number. The display is updated only when io_6 changes, so current and temperature are never shown.
Item button edges set selectedItem and call showItemAndPrice, which displays item digit*1000+price on the TM1637.
On D7 release with selection, dispenseItem checks stock>0, prints dispense:itemX, decrements stock, and beeps.
When stock is zero, dispenseItem prints error, shows error code on display, and alarms with repeated beeps.
Holding D7 past LONG_PRESS_MS sets adminMode true with display/LED/beep feedback.
In admin mode serial lines are read and processAdminCommand handles add/stock commands updating stockArr for the parsed item.

setup() initializes button, LEDs, buzzer, TM1637, and both ultrasonic trigger/echo pins, and loop() continuously samples sensors and drives display/LEDs/buzzer via ProgramPage1, showing distance/occupancy by mode.

Green LED (D10) is driven by io_2, which is set to true when parking sensor is not valid and entrance approach io_5 is true (or parking distance >=5), i.e., vehicle near entrance with no car in spot lights green.
When parking sensor valid (io_7), buzzer frequency is graded by distance: <5cm 2000, 2-10cm 1200, 10-30cm 800, >=30cm 400, and red LED io_1 is set when parking valid and distance >=5.
When parking valid and distance <5cm, buzzer command is 2000 Hz continuously (tone held until command changes), satisfying continuous alarm.
Button D2 with edge detection cycles mode 0->1->2->0; display value selects entrance distance (mode0 & approach), parking distance (mode1 & valid), or occupancy count (mode2).
setup() initializes serial, the three sensor pins as inputs, buzzer pin 6, LED pin 13, and the TM1637 display (CLK=4, DIO=5), then loop() runs the model each cycle.
The model computes a layer count from the three inputs via nested conditionals (0-3) and writes it to io_5, which is the display value.
loop() writes the computed count (hw_value_io_5) to the TM1637 via showNumberDec when it changes.
No timing/elapsed tracking exists for per-layer vacancy; restock_needed is hardcoded false and query_elapsed_ms is hardcoded 0, so no 'long empty' condition can ever trigger restock needed.

The all-full branch sets a 1000 tone value but the buzzer command is gated to 31-65535, so 1000 is valid; however the 'lock new records' output is hardcoded false and no locking state is implemented, and the tone is only a momentary value not a persistent lock. The lock_new_records output is always false.

Serial output is only emitted when serial_0_trigger is true, but trigger is derived from 'not all full and previousAllFull' edge, not from any serial query command; there is no Serial.read/parse of query commands, so a query cannot produce layer status output.
No serial command parsing or timer reset logic exists; query_elapsed_ms is hardcoded 0 and there is no code reading serial input to reset any timing.

Exit sensor (index 1) rising first sets EXIT_FIRST; subsequent entry sensor rise calls finishPassage(false) which decrements occupancy.
Button debounce toggles showTemperature on LOW press; serviceDisplay then renders temperature segments instead of count.
updateFan computes PWM from temperature (clamped 18-32) plus occupancy*4 with base 80 when occupancy nonzero, writing to FAN_PWM_PIN.
When occupancy is 0, requestedPwm stays 0 and analogWrite sets fan to 0; status reports ENERGY_SAVE.
Source assigns DISPLAY_DIO to D3, not D5, so there is no pin conflict in the code; the requirement's D5/DIO conflict is not present in the implementation.

setup() configures all required pins (A0, A1, D2 pullup, D5 output, D6 output, D13 output, D4 CLK, D3 DIO) and Serial.begin(9600); loop() continuously samples sensors, vibration, and updates state/outputs.
When no fault flags are set, nextState resolves to NORMAL; printStateName prints NORMAL and LED is set HIGH.
currentRmsA >= OVERLOAD_ON_A sets overloadActive, and with no higher-priority fault nextState becomes OVERLOAD, printed as OVERLOAD.
temperatureC >= OVERHEAT_ON_C sets overheatActive, nextState becomes OVERHEAT (when no mechanical fault), and fanPwm is computed and written to FAN_PIN via analogWrite.
Vibration LOW sets mechanicalActive; nextState becomes MECHANICAL_FAULT, buzzer beeps at 2400Hz, and printTelemetry outputs FAULT=F0<state> with state 3.
The ternary chain prioritizes mechanicalActive over overheatActive and overloadActive, so MECHANICAL_FAULT wins when simultaneous; buzzer and fault code follow that state.
displayPage cycles 0,1,2 every DISPLAY_PAGE_MS; page 0 shows current (A), page 1 shows temperature (C), page 2 shows state number S0x.
manualMode toggled by D2 button; updateOutputs selects manual vs automatic values based on manualMode, so both modes exist.
Temperature from DHT11 drives autoFanOn hysteresis and PWM computed from temperatureC, written to FAN_PIN (D5) via analogWrite.
Light percent from A0 drives autoLEDOn and PWM written to LED_PIN (D9).
Soil percent from A1 drives autoPumpOn, which is passed to updatePump controlling PUMP_PIN (D10) relay.
D3 button in manual mode cycles selectedItem through FAN/LED/PUMP.

Display page cycles 0/1/2 every 2s showing temperature, light, soil respectively via setSegments.
Any fault sets fault true; updateAlarm toggles tone on BUZZER_PIN (D6) when fault active.

Init sets modeIsSetting=false (current-value mode default) and loop runs ProgramPage1 each cycle; temperature control and fan toggling are implemented in the update body.
Heater output io_1 is true when not alarm and valid temp below targetTemp; D10 driven from io_1.

Fan state toggles each valid DHT sample when not alarmed, and D5 is driven from fanOn.
Rising-edge button toggles modeIsSetting, which selects target vs current value for display.
When not in setting mode, display value is derived from tempLastValid and shown on TM1637.
When modeIsSetting, display value is derived from targetTemp and shown on TM1637.

High-abnormal counter increments per loop iteration (~10ms), reaching 6000 in ~60s only if loop timing holds; but the alarm threshold is 6000 counts, not a verified 1-minute timer, and the serial output prints 'incubation_abnormal' with a boolean suffix rather than 'incubation abnormal'. The counter is also reset whenever DHT read is invalid, and the high condition uses >=38 while low uses <=36, leaving a gap. The serial string does not match the required text.

setup initializes displayTemperature=false and peopleCount=0, then modelTick sets io_8=peopleCount and applyOutputs calls showNumberDec(io_8), so default display shows count.
modelTick unconditionally assigns peopleCount to 0 in every branch regardless of io_0/io_2/io_3 ordering; no increment path exists, so entry-first cannot increase count.

Button edge toggles displayTemperature; modelTick then sets io_8 to floor(io_4) when displayTemperature and io_6 valid, and applyOutputs displays io_8.
Fan PWM is computed from peopleCount and io_4 temperature thresholds (255/180/120/60) and written to FAN_PWM_PIN via analogWrite.

setup() initializes the model, Serial, button pins 2/3/7 as inputs, LED 13, buzzer 6, and TM1637 on pins 4/5; init sets stageIndex=0 and paused=true, entering the settable three-stage state.
On rising edge of io_0 (D2), the current stage's remaining time is incremented by 1000 ms based on stageIndex.
On rising edge of io_1 (D3), stageIndex advances by one, wrapping from 2 to 0, switching the stage being configured.
On rising edge of io_2 (D7) when not completed, paused is set to !paused; starting from paused=true sets paused=false, beginning the countdown.
Same toggle: when running (paused=false), pressing io_2 sets paused=true, pausing the countdown.

Stage transitions occur when remaining<=0, but no code decrements remaining time, no buzzer beep pattern is generated (io_4 is always 0), and no per-stage beep count exists. The transition also does not reset the next stage's remaining time.

When stage3 remaining<=0, completed is set true, and io_3=completed drives D13 HIGH, so LED does turn on at completion. However the requirement is met only if stages actually complete; since remaining times are never decremented, completion never occurs. The LED-on path itself is implemented.

Serial prints occur when completed, but the elapsed values (stage1/2/3ElapsedMs, totalElapsedMs) are never updated anywhere, so they always print 0; also the string is 'process_complete_total_ms' not 'process complete'.

On stable reset press, resetSystem(false) sets locked=false and clears winner/display, restoring ready state.
When reset held >=3000ms, resetSystem(true) zeroes totalBets for all four contestants.
setup() initializes serial, PIR D2, door D3, LDR A0, buzzer D6, LED D13, and TM1637 constructed with CLK=4/DIO=5 with brightness set.
nightAuto is set each step from analogRead(A0) below 512, and the alarm/event logic treats armed OR nightAuto as the armed condition, so low light auto-arms.
When armed/nightAuto and door rising and PIR rising, eventCount increments, buzzer tone 2000 and LED output are driven, and eventCount is shown on TM1637.

At startup peopleCount=0 and displayTemperature=false, so the display value is set to peopleCount and shown on the TM1637 in setup and loop.
When entry sensor (io_1) is triggered, both branches of the io_3 check assign peopleCount to 0 regardless of prior count, so no increment occurs.
When only the exit sensor (io_3) is triggered without entry, peopleCount is set to 0 rather than decremented.
Button D2 toggles displayTemperature on rising edge, and the display value switches to the integer temperature when displayTemperature is true.

When peopleCount is 0, fan value is set to 0.0 and eco_mode serial flag is true; analogWrite outputs 0.
Fan PWM uses pin 5 and TM1637 is constructed with DIO pin 3 (CLK 4), so there is no D5 conflict in the actual code.
setup() initializes Serial and configures pins for IR (D2 input), valve (D10 output), TM1637 (D4/D5 via constructor), buzzer (D6 output), LED (D13 output), and ultrasonic (D8 output, D9 input).

The valve output io_1 is set true only while near is active and level>=10; there is no fixed-duration timer that keeps the valve open for a set time after detection. The valve closes as soon as proximity ends, so the required fixed-duration open behavior is not implemented.
When near is true and level<10, io_5 (tone) is set to 2000 and io_1 (valve) remains false, so the valve is blocked and the buzzer alarms.

The TM1637 only displays io_4, which is the remaining water percentage. The today usage count (io_5 is tone, count is sysml_value_5/serial only) is never sent to the display, so the required usage count display is missing.
Serial output is gated by serial_0_trigger, which is hardcoded to false (if(false)), so no statistics are ever printed. There is also no serial query parsing.
setup() configures Serial, pin 2 input, pin 10 output, TM1637 on pins 4/5, pin 6 output, pin 13 output, and HC-SR04 trig 8/echo 9, matching the wiring.
Valve output io_1 is only true while near AND level>=20; it is not latched for a fixed duration, so it closes as soon as proximity ends. No timer holds the valve open for a fixed time.
When near and level<20, valve output is false (io_1=0) and buzzer value io_5 is set to 2000 Hz, driving tone on pin 6.
The TM1637 only displays a single number (io_4 = remaining percent). The today usage count (io_5) is routed to the buzzer/tone output, not to the display, so both values are not shown.

Serial output is gated on serial_0_trigger which equals io_0 (proximity), not on any serial query/command. There is no reading of Serial input to trigger statistics, so a serial query does not produce stats.

Selection updates selectedItemIndex, but the display only shows the item number (1/2/3), never the price; no price data exists anywhere. The requirement to show both number and price is not implemented.

On confirm with stock, stock decrements and a beep occurs, but the serial output is 'dispense:itemX code=1001' rather than the required exact 'dispense:itemX'. The extra token violates the required output text.

When stock is insufficient, the display shows error code 901/902/903, but the serial path still prints 'dispense:itemX code=901' instead of an alarm/error indication; the buzzer beep is the same as success and no distinct alarm is produced. The error is not clearly reported as an alarm.

Long-press D7 is not distinguished from short press; any D7 press immediately sets adminMode true on the same tick, so a short confirm press also enters admin mode. There is no long-press timing logic.
Serial input is drained and discarded; no parsing or stock update occurs, so replenishment via serial is not implemented.

No water-level comparison or alarm logic exists; io_5 (buzzer) is hardcoded 0 and pump is unconditionally off, so no alarm is produced on low water.
Button edge detection toggles sysml_state_manualMode on press, implementing auto/manual switching.

locked is set true on winner and shouldTriggerWinner returns false while locked; only resetSystem (called from reset handler) clears locked.

D7 is treated as a level, not a long press: any HIGH on io_3 immediately sets adminMode true, so a short press also enters admin mode. There is no duration measurement for long-press detection.

Initial state is CONFIGURING, not the preheat stage; the process only enters stage 1 (preheat) after a start action (D2 hold or START command). At boot the system is in configuration mode, not preheating.

isChargingLike compares voltageAdc against a threshold and the result drives the TM1637 charge display, so charging state is derived from the A2 voltage reading.
Falling-edge press on D2 toggles autoMode, and autoMode selects between the two servo control branches.

Compares io_0 (A0) vs io_1 (A1); if A0>A1 sets 45 else 135, and loop writes that angle to servo D9.
Reads A2 into io_2 and sets chargingLowActive based on threshold comparison, deriving charging state from voltage.
Button D2 read into io_3; edge detection toggles autoMode between true/false on press.

Buzzer and serial trigger are driven directly by instantaneous chargingLowActive (io_2<500), with no persistence/timing for 'long-term' low voltage; also serial prints 'low charge' concatenated with '1' rather than the required message.

Button edges set pendingMask and trigger serial output, but activeWaitSeconds is never incremented (line 197 is a self-assignment) and serialElapsedMs/serialWaitS are reset to 0 and never updated, so no waiting time is recorded. Also the serial trigger is cleared at the start of the next ProgramPage1 call (line 100) before the loop prints, so the alarm/log output is effectively suppressed.

The D7 edge clears pendingMask and sets activeBedIndex=0, but the serial trigger is latched then cleared at the start of the next update before loop prints, so no processing log is output. Also the 'highest priority' clearing only handles single-bit masks and does not clear the corresponding bed's wait state coherently.

The display value is activeBedIndex*100 + activeWaitSeconds, but activeWaitSeconds is never incremented (stays 0), so the seconds portion is always 00. Additionally activeBedIndex is overwritten by the most recent call rather than the longest-waiting bed, so it does not show the longest-waiting bed's number and seconds.
